claims: An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is the process where a private company raises capital by selling shares to the public for the first time, transitioning into a public entity.
Companies hire investment banks (underwriters) to manage the offering.
Companies hire investment banks (underwriters) to assess valuation.
Companies hire investment banks (underwriters) to handle regulatory compliance.
The company files a registration statement (Form S-1) with the SEC.
The registration statement (Form S-1) includes financial data and business plans.
Management markets the company to institutional investors to gauge demand (roadshow).
Management sets the final IPO price with underwriters.
Shares begin trading on a public exchange (e.g., NYSE or Nasdaq).
SEC requirements for disclosure include audited financial statements.
